issues.legal_issue: A categorical admission in a pleading cannot be wholly withdrawn by amending the pleading.
material_facts: The defendants repeatedly stated in an affidavit and written statement that their predecessor had separated from the family and relinquished his interest in the disputed property, and that they had no interest in it.
About twenty-five years after the written statement, the defendants sought to amend it to resile from those admissions.
The defendants had also commenced a separate suit challenging the alleged relinquishment.
issues.conclusion: The application to amend the written statement so as to wholly withdraw the admissions was rejected; the decision allowing that amendment was modified.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a categorical admission in a pleading cannot be withdrawn by amendment, although it may be explained or clarified. Judicial admissions, admissible under Section 58 of the Evidence Act, stand on a higher footing than evidentiary admissions and can themselves found the rights of the parties. The Court relied on Nagindas Ramdas v. Dalpatram Ichharam and Gautam Sarup v. Leela Jetly, and overruled Panchdeo Narain Srivastava v. Km. Jyoti Sahay to the extent it held that an admission could be withdrawn. Modi Spinning and Weaving Mills Co. Ltd. v. Ladha Ram & Co. also supports refusing an amendment that displaces the opposing party from an admission.

predicates.amendment_application_in_pending_suit: A party applied to amend its pleading in a pending suit.
predicates.categorical_pleading_admission: The party made a clear admission of fact in its pleading.
predicates.amendment_wholly_retracts_admission: The proposed amendment would wholly resile from, rather than explain or clarify, the admission.

issues.definition: When a party seeks in a pending suit to amend its pleading so as to wholly retract a clear factual admission, that admission cannot be wholly withdrawn by amendment.

issues.legal_issue: A party may seek to amend a pleading to explain or clarify an admission without wholly withdrawing it.
material_facts: The defendants said their amendment was intended to explain the circumstances in which a letter referring to relinquishment had been written, rather than to resile from the letter or their earlier pleading about it.
The Court rejected the proposed amendment insofar as it withdrew the admissions, but permitted the defendants to apply to explain or clarify them.
issues.conclusion: The defendants were permitted to file an application limited to explaining or clarifying the disputed admissions, to be considered on its merits in light of the Court's observations.
issues.legal_principle: Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits amendment of pleadings, and a categorical admission may be explained or clarified even though it cannot be wholly withdrawn. The Court relied on Gautam Sarup v. Leela Jetly and distinguished the principle concerning withdrawal in Panchdeo Narain Srivastava. An alternative plea may be available, but alternative pleas cannot be mutually destructive of one another.

predicates.amendment_application_in_pending_suit: A party applied to amend its pleading in a pending suit.
predicates.pleading_contains_admission: The pleading contains an admission of fact by the party seeking amendment.
predicates.proposed_amendment_explains_or_clarifies: The proposed amendment supplies an explanation or clarification of the admission rather than wholly retracting it.

issues.definition: A party seeking to explain or clarify an admission in a pleading may apply to amend that pleading, with the request considered on its merits.

issues.legal_issue: Delay alone does not determine whether an amendment to a written statement should be permitted.
material_facts: The defendants sought amendment about twenty-five years after filing their written statement.
Issues in the suit had been framed only in 2009, and the Court considered the nature and character of the proposed amendment and the surrounding circumstances as relevant to the delay.
issues.conclusion: Delay by itself was not decisive; the nature and character of the amendment and the other circumstances had to be considered, although the proposed wholesale withdrawal of the admissions was impermissible.
issues.legal_principle: In considering an application under Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, delay is not by itself crucial. The court must consider the nature and character of the amendment and the circumstances of the case, along with the established amendment principles summarized in Revajeetu Builders and Developers v. Narayanaswamy and Sons, including bona fides, prejudice, injustice, and the effect on the nature of the case.

predicates.amendment_application_in_pending_suit: A party applied to amend a pleading in a pending suit.
predicates.amendment_is_delayed: The party applied to amend after a substantial period had passed since filing the pleading.

issues.definition: In a delayed amendment application in a pending suit, delay alone does not determine whether the amendment should be allowed.

issues.legal_issue: The basis of an admission may be challenged in a substantive proceeding even though the admission cannot be wholly withdrawn by amendment.
material_facts: After seeking to amend their written statement, the defendants filed a separate suit challenging the arbitration award and the alleged relinquishment on which the admissions rested.
The Court declined to make that separate suit infructuous while rejecting the proposed amendment that would wholly withdraw the admissions.
issues.conclusion: The basis of an admission may be attacked in a substantive proceeding; the Court did not determine the merits or outcome of the separate suit.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished wholly withdrawing a categorical admission by amendment from challenging the basis of that admission in substantive proceedings. Its reliance on Nagindas Ramdas v. Dalpatram Ichharam and Gautam Sarup v. Leela Jetly concerned the binding character of categorical admissions in pleadings, while recognizing that the basis of an admission may be attacked separately.

predicates.substantive_proceeding_challenges_basis_: A party brings a substantive proceeding to contest the factual or legal basis on which an admission rests.
predicates.pleading_admission_is_not_wholly_withdra: The party does not use an amendment to wholly withdraw the admission in the pending pleading.

issues.definition: A party may challenge the basis of an admission through a substantive proceeding while leaving the admission unwithdrawn by amendment.
